map.Steady is provable. Mean first: add the: We can prove it is steady. Mean first: add the days, share the total equally. Then measure the wobble.
map.The wobble has a name: mean absolute dev: The wobble has a name: mean absolute deviation. MAD = the average distance from each data point to the mean. Small MAD: calm data. Large MAD: a wild ride.
map.A deviation is a distance from the mean: A deviation is a distance from the mean. It is always positive. Average the distances to get the MAD.
Reader, you do the consistency check. Mean first, then MAD.
map.Rosa's five days: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 tra: Rosa's five days: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 trays. Step 1: find the mean. The deviation chips will fill in. Step 2: average the five deviations to find the MAD.
map.Conceptual: the mean is the fair-share n: Conceptual: the mean is the fair-share number. Put all five days together, then share the total equally. A deviation is a DISTANCE from the mean, so it is never negative.
map.Procedural: pair the smallest day with t: Procedural: pair the smallest day with the largest. Pair the next-smallest with the next-largest. Equal sums make dividing by 5 quick. For the MAD: add the five deviation chips. Then divide that total by 5.
map.There's the lawyer's whole case: one par: That is the lawyer's whole case: one parade-day tower. An outlier is a value far from all the rest.
map.Rule of evidence: an outlier drags the m: Rule of evidence: an outlier pulls the mean toward itself. It also stretches the range. The median and the IQR only use the middle of the line-up. They do not move.
map.Choosing a measure is a math decision: m: Choosing a measure is a math choice: match the measure to the data's shape. Skewed data or outliers? Use measures based on the middle.
map.Two calls to make before the hearing. Pi: Two choices before the hearing. Pick the most honest measure for each job.
map.Conceptual: ask what each measure listen: Conceptual: ask what each measure uses. Some use EVERY value, even the spike. Others use only the middle of the ordered list, so one wild day cannot move them.
map.Procedural: Scenario A — cross off every: Procedural: Scenario A: cross off every measure an outlier can pull (the mean, the maximum) or that ignores what is typical. Scenario B: the full stretch goes end to end, right through the outlier. Pick the spread that uses the middle half of the data.

map.Conceptual: MAD measures wobble — small: Conceptual: MAD measures wobble. Small MAD means hours close to the mean. Big MAD means wild swings. 'Consistent' means LESS wobble, not more sales.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — compare the two MAD: Procedural: Lock 1: compare the two MADs. The smaller one is more consistent. Lock 2: on a typical hour, Rosa is off the mean by about her own MAD. Lock 3: an honest closing uses BOTH numbers: center for 'typical,' spread for 'trustworthy.'

map.MAD.Find the mean, measure each value's: MAD.Find the mean. Find each value's distance from it. Then average those distances. Small MAD = steady data.
map.Choosing center.One huge outlier drags t: Choosing center.One huge outlier pulls the mean. The median stays put. Use it when data is skewed.
map.Choosing spread.Range and MAD feel an ou: Choosing spread.Range and MAD are changed by an outlier. The IQR uses only the middle 50%, so it stays steady.
map.The honest number.Center tells you the t: The honest number.Center tells you the typical value. Spread tells you how much to trust it. Report both.
